scams.name: The Susukino Hustler Bar Rip-Off (Bottakuri)
scams.description: Street hustlers in Susukino approach visitors claiming to warn about rip-off bars, then lead them to overpriced venues where hidden charges, inflated drink prices, and mandatory fees accumulate rapidly. A documented case involved a ¥343,200 tab including champagne priced over ¥200,000 per bottle. Victims report being blocked from leaving until payment is made or cards are surrendered.
scams.avoidance: Never follow street hustlers or use free information booths in Susukino, as both are illegal under the 2022 ordinance. Pick bars in advance via Tabelog or Google Maps. Ask about seating charges and request full menus before sitting. Pay cash only, keep cards and passport secure, photograph menus, and call 110 if trapped.
scams.location: Susukino entertainment district, especially Minami 5-6 jo / Nishi 4-5 chome, near Remonya and City Boys buildings

scams.name: The Host Club Tsukebarai (Tab-Debt) Trap for Women
scams.description: Host clubs and men's concept cafes target female customers with romantic manipulation, encouraging high-spending tsukebarai (tab/credit) debts. Once debt accumulates beyond ability to pay, clubs refer customers to illegal sex-work brokers. A 2024 investigation documented seven arrests involving a ring earning over ¥100 million annually through this scheme.
scams.avoidance: Never accept tsukebarai tabs; leave immediately if unable to pay in cash. Treat romantic overtures as sales scripts. Set nightly cash limits, leave cards at hotels, and refuse champagne tower invitations. If offered 'easier work' or referred to sex shops, contact Hokkaido Police sex-crime line at 0120-028-110.
scams.location: Susukino host clubs and men's concept cafes, concentrated on Minami 6-8 jo / Nishi 4-5 chome

scams.name: The Nijo Market "Inbound-Don" Overcharge
scams.description: Nijo Market restaurants charge tourists ¥3,000-¥4,000 for mediocre kaisendon bowls that cost ¥1,500-¥2,500 elsewhere, and ¥500 per mantis shrimp when Daimaru sells two for ¥600. English and Chinese menus signal inflated pricing; local-language prices are absent or minimized.
scams.avoidance: Visit Jogai (Central Wholesale Outer) Market near Sapporo Station instead, where prices are roughly half. If eating at Nijo, use only Japanese-language menus and confirm total price beforehand. Buy crab at New Chitose Airport duty-free, bring cash, and budget no more than ¥2,500 for kaisendon.
scams.location: Nijo Ichiba (二条市場), Minami 3-jo Higashi 1-2-chome, near Tanukikoji; also Jogai Ichiba

scams.name: The Susukino Crab-Buffet "All You Can Eat" Trap
scams.description: Tourist-chain crab restaurants advertise ¥6,000-¥10,000 all-you-can-eat buffets where the first serving is fresh but subsequent plates are lower-grade or near-spoiled. Staff dig through trash to enforce finish-the-plate policies, use strict timers to force drink orders, and serve frozen product despite 'live' claims.
scams.avoidance: Skip tour-bus chains like Nanda, Ebi-Kani-Gassen, and Kani Shogun. Book small à-la-carte crab specialists where quality can be judged per dish. Read recent Google 1-star reviews before booking. Buy vacuum-sealed crab at New Chitose Airport instead. Bring cash and confirm total pricing beforehand.
scams.location: Susukino, particularly at major tourist-facing crab restaurant chains

scams.name: The Ramen Yokocho Tourist-Alley Bait-and-Switch
scams.description: Ganso Sapporo Ramen Yokocho's 17 shops charge ¥1,200-¥1,500 for miso ramen versus ¥900-¥1,100 nearby. Service to foreigners is dismissive, toppings are frozen, and shops close unpredictably or refuse walk-ins despite empty seats. One review documented a blue glove fragment in broth.
scams.avoidance: Skip the famous alley; visit Sumire, Ramen Shingen, Menya Saimi, or ramen shops at New Chitose Airport instead. If visiting Yokocho, check individual shop Google reviews from the last six months. Avoid shops with aggressive hosts outside. Visit before 11:30 AM or after 2 PM to avoid tour buses.
scams.location: Ganso Sapporo Ramen Yokocho and Shin Ramen Yokocho, Minami 5-jo Nishi 3-chome, Susukino

scams.name: The "Free Information Booth" (無料案内所) Kickback Scheme
scams.description: Neon-signed 'Free Information' kiosks throughout Susukino are commission-paid referral agencies, not tourist information offices. They direct clients to partner bars paying the highest commissions regardless of customer requests. Final bills do not match brochure prices, and the booth becomes unreachable when complaints arise.
scams.avoidance: Never use 無料案内所 booths; use Google Maps, Tabelog, or HOT PEPPER Gourmet instead. Book venues directly via their websites or phone numbers. Walk alone to chosen venues and refuse escorts from booth staff. Call consumer hotline 188 for misrepresentation complaints.
scams.location: Susukino, concentrated in Minami 5-6 jo / Nishi 3-5 chome around main Susukino crossing

scams.name: The Sapporo Hotel-Parking Non-Refund Trap
scams.description: Rental SUVs and minivans are rejected by hotel mechanical stackers due to size limits. Hotels refuse refunds of pre-booked parking fees and offer no alternative arrangements, leaving drivers to pay ¥1,500+ nightly at other lots while losing the original hotel parking fee.
scams.avoidance: Email hotels directly before booking to confirm exact vehicle length, height, and weight limits for stackers. Stay near Sapporo Station at hotels with surface lots. Drop rentals at the airport and take the Rapid Airport train (¥1,150, 37 min). Use public paid lots instead of hotel parking.
scams.location: Central Sapporo hotels (Chuo-ku), particularly those without on-site parking garages
